essential_protocols: OR-Set row membership with add/remove tags
Per-cell MV-registers for independent column merges
Vector-clock max merge with dominance checks
Post-merge uniqueness grouping with deterministic arbitration
Conflict log for recoverable uniqueness losers
Tombstone FK policy with chain repair after writes/imports
Idempotent pairwise sync and deterministic snapshot hashing

results.reason:
• Reference: Duplicate users, a parent delete, an order pointing at that deleted user, and concurrent column updates are merged across three peers.
• Risk: The scenario fails to handle the interaction between cell-level updates, FK policies, and uniqueness constraints.
• Mechanism: Rows are merged using OR-Set add/remove tags, and cells are merged by synchronizing MV-register clocks, with deterministic arbitration resolving email collisions.
• Causal note: The lack of dominance in concurrent cell updates ensures that write operations are preserved independently before visible values are chosen.
• Result: The assertions passed for convergence, uniqueness of users.email, tombstone detection, and cell-level update u1, with some potential issues with FK policy propagation and repair.

• Case: Two peers update different columns of the same observed row while offline. 
• Risk: A row-level last-writer-wins merge would keep one update and erase the other.
• Mechanism: Each column's MV-register ensures that updates are merged independently, avoiding row-level competition.
• Causal note: The lack of dominance ensures that both updates are preserved, as each column's write is not dependent on the other.
• Result: Convergence and cell-level-strict assertions passed, demonstrating post-merge grouping and deterministic winner selection through independent column updates.

• Case: The reference trace is replayed, but final sync pairs are shuffled by seed.
• Risk: Order-sensitive metadata can cause peers to converge per seed but produce different hashes across seeds.
• Mechanism: Merge uses max vector-clock entries, add/remove tag union, and recomputes conflicts from the merged state.
• Causal note: Clocks and dominance are critical to resolving conflicts correctly after shuffle.
• Result: Convergence and order-invariance pass, but the shuffle introduces variability in hash values.

• stretch:composite_uniqueness:
  • Case: Peers insert memberships that collide on `(user_id, team_id)` while offline, causing rows to be grouped by the full composite key.
  • Risk: Single-column uniqueness logic may drop losing rows due to tuple collisions.
  • Mechanism: One deterministic winner remains on the original tuple, with losers retained with conflict-safe rewritten unique values.
  • Causal note: Row clocks and stable tie-breaks ensure peers choose the same row after exchanging histories.
  • Result: The system passes assertions for convergence, composite uniqueness, and data preservation.

stretch:multi_level_fk:
• Case: When the organization root is deleted, users and orders beneath it are created or learned on other peers.
• Risk: FK handling can stop after one level, leaving users or orders pointing at deleted parents.
• Mechanism: After every write/import, FK repair walks the full organization -> users -> orders chain, applying the tombstone policy to ensure data integrity.
• Causal note: Repair only reacts to known deletes or tombstones, not to pending child removals.
• Result: The scenario passes with convergence, fk-chain-integrity, and data-preservation, but may fail on data-preservation due to potential post-merge grouping inconsistencies and deterministic winner selection issues.

• Case: Six peers insert the same email concurrently, alongside non-conflicting users.
• Risk: A replace-style implementation may silently delete most inserts.
• Mechanism: Post-merge grouping by email selects one deterministic winner, while preserving original emails in the conflict log.
• Causal note: Stable clocks are needed due to concurrent inserts, as tie-breaks can't rely on arrival order.
• Result: The scenario passed assertions on convergence, uniqueness of user emails, data preservation, and deterministic winner selection.
